episodes.title: What is Geography?
episodes.description: Use the banana trade to uncover the broader histories and connections behind geographic facts.

episodes.title: What is a Map?
episodes.description: Compare map types, projections, and the decisions cartographers make when representing the world.

episodes.title: What is space and how do we study it?
episodes.description: Explore different understandings of geographic space and tools for investigating it.

episodes.title: What is Physical Geography?
episodes.description: Introduce environmental processes and the relationship between physical landscapes and human activity.

episodes.title: How Does the Earth Move?
episodes.description: Connect Earth's origins, rotation, tilt, and orbit with patterns that shape its environments.

episodes.title: What Does the Atmosphere Do?
episodes.description: Explore atmospheric layers, incoming sunlight, and the protective and warming effects of the air around Earth.

episodes.title: How Does Air Temperature Shape a Place?
episodes.description: Use Siberia to investigate how temperature shapes communities, economies, and landscapes.

episodes.title: Where Does Wind Come From?
episodes.description: Explore wind formation, global pressure patterns, and the deflection caused by Earth's rotation.

episodes.title: How Do Oceans Circulate?
episodes.description: Follow discarded plastic to investigate ocean currents, circulation, and the movement of nutrients and goods.

episodes.title: What is a Cloud?
episodes.description: Investigate cloud formation, rainfall, humidity, and what clouds reveal about weather patterns.

episodes.title: How Can Rain Create Conflict? Precipitation and Water Use
episodes.description: Connect rainfall and population with conflicts over water across the American West and Great Plains.

episodes.title: What Are the Different Types of Cyclones?
episodes.description: Compare the formation and impacts of tropical cyclones and large midlatitude weather systems.

episodes.title: How do we Classify Climates?
episodes.description: Follow the potato's history while exploring climate classification and human adaptation.

episodes.title: What is Climate Change?
episodes.description: Compare natural and human influences on long-term weather patterns and recent global warming.

episodes.title: What Are Ecosystems?
episodes.description: Explore ecosystem energy, nutrient cycling, and the patterns that distinguish major biomes.

episodes.title: Population & Food
episodes.description: Connect food chains, consumption patterns, population growth, and Earth's capacity to support people.

episodes.title: What is Soil (and Why is it Important)?
episodes.description: Explore soil ingredients, layers, and environmental differences that support ecosystems and agriculture.

episodes.title: What Are Rocks and How Do They Form?
episodes.description: Follow granite through the rock cycle to uncover geological stories spanning millions of years.

episodes.title: The Plate Tectonics Revolution
episodes.description: Trace the evidence and international scientific work behind the theory of moving plates.

episodes.title: How Does the Earth Create Different Landforms?
episodes.description: Explore how changing landforms influence settlement, cultural meaning, and people's sense of place.

episodes.title: What are Volcanoes?
episodes.description: Compare volcanic types and patterns of eruptions around the world.

episodes.title: What is Weathering?
episodes.description: Distinguish mechanical, biological, and chemical processes that break rock into sediment.

episodes.title: How Rivers Shape the Landscape
episodes.description: Follow the Zambezi to examine river features, changing channels, waterfalls, and deltas.

episodes.title: Why Does Jakarta Flood So Easily?
episodes.description: Investigate Jakarta's flooding and the protective and filtering roles of mangroves and wetlands.

episodes.title: Groundwater and the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict
episodes.description: Explore how groundwater access and political boundaries complicate relations between Israelis and Palestinians.

episodes.title: What are Glaciers?
episodes.description: Investigate glaciers as landscape-shaping forces and records of changing climates.

episodes.title: Natural Hazards
episodes.description: Distinguish physical hazards from human disasters and examine how geographers assess their impacts.

episodes.title: What is Human Geography?
episodes.description: Explore human-environment relationships through place names, political power, and changing perceptions of space.

episodes.title: Race, Ethnicity, and the Cultural Landscape
episodes.description: Investigate cultural landscapes and the relationships among ethnicity, racial categories, and power.

episodes.title: How Does Language Move?
episodes.description: Explore language as an identity marker and a way that cultural traits travel.

episodes.title: How Did Religion Spread Along the Silk Road?
episodes.description: Follow religious beliefs along the Silk Roads to examine how trade routes spread ideas.

episodes.title: Where and Why Do People Move?
episodes.description: Use the Indian diaspora to compare voluntary and forced movement and its wider geographic effects.

episodes.title: How Populations Grow and Change
episodes.description: Explore population change, resource limits, and competing accounts of how societies support growing numbers.

episodes.title: How Does Disease Move?
episodes.description: Learn how medical geographers track illness and environmental exposures across landscapes.

episodes.title: Tyranny of the Map
episodes.description: Examine how imposed boundaries can conflict with communities and produce lasting political tensions.

episodes.title: What Holds a Country Together or Tears it Apart?
episodes.description: Compare Latin American examples to explore forces that unite countries or pull them apart.

episodes.title: What are the Patterns of Border Conflicts?
episodes.description: Read changing borders and territorial shapes as evidence of conflict and shifting power.

episodes.title: Capitalism, Communism, & Political Economies
episodes.description: Trace Bulgaria and Germany to investigate how political systems shape economic outcomes.

episodes.title: Colonialism
episodes.description: Explore lasting effects of colonial domination and the power to shape cultural narratives.

episodes.title: What is a “Developed” Country?
episodes.description: Question wealth-centered definitions of development and consider sustainability, history, and well-being.

episodes.title: Agribusiness, GMOs, and their Role in Development
episodes.description: Investigate genetically modified cotton and its relationship with India's agricultural crisis.

episodes.title: Why is There Uneven Access to Food?
episodes.description: Connect unequal food access with historical exchanges and changes in agricultural technology.

episodes.title: How Do We Produce Food?
episodes.description: Compare subsistence, smaller-scale, and industrial farming through agricultural history in the Philippines.

episodes.title: Mineral Extraction
episodes.description: Use mineral extraction in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to examine interconnected geographic impacts.

episodes.title: Why are People Moving to Cities?
episodes.description: Investigate migration toward cities and the historical structures that influence urban patterns.

episodes.title: How are Cities Organized?
episodes.description: Compare models of urban organization and the historical development of districts and communities.

episodes.title: What is Urban Planning?
episodes.description: Explore how city planning combines economic, environmental, and social priorities in shaping people's lives.

episodes.title: How did Detroit Become the Motor City? (Industrial Geography)
episodes.description: Trace the American automotive industry through transport networks, resource access, and industrial location.

episodes.title: Sustainable Cities
episodes.description: Explore environmental planning and how sustainable-city ambitions intersect with existing communities.

episodes.title: Geographies of the Future
episodes.description: Revisit space, place, and human-environment connections while considering digital worlds and future geography.
